title: Completeness of any coefficient tower limit
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $T$ a scheme in the same universe, $D$ its abelian coefficient-tower presentation, and $C\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(B_n))$ any derived tower [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. If $M,p,\delta$ is a distinguished Roos triangle for its completed evaluations with their actual transitions [def-sp-tower-reconstruction-data, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], then $M$ is derived complete in the exact quotient-unit sense of [def-weil-derived-complete]. No normalization, constructibility, or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Proof completeness sentence, expanded steps 9--10; comparison with the recorded canonical quotient unit.

proof.text: Choose a single semilinear flat-term K-flat tower model. Restrict its strict transitions to completed coefficients. Write ell=v*pi^e, e>=1. Level n is killed termwise by pi^(en), allowing a torsion exponent depending on n.

Apply the power-torsion sheaf-limit theorem. Each row completion unit is invertible after its own cutoff, and signed interchange of the two Roos directions proves the limit unit invertible. Its quotient comparison preserves all quotient-unit projections.

Using a common K-flat resolution, identify the quotient reductions and their unit maps with sfDerivedReductionUnit and the uniquely characterized sfDerivedReductionTransition. Transport the resulting distinguished quotient Roos triangle along the completed model lift and the isomorphism of the two Roos presentations. This is exactly IsSfDerivedComplete.
